function: Learns AP active beamforming and STAR-RIS amplitude and phase control (multi-agent PPO with imitation of SCA solutions); association, pairing and decoding order are classical (pp. 8-12).
system: 3 APs with 4 antennas each, 20 single-antenna UEs, 4 STAR-RIS units (energy splitting, 26 elements), NOMA downlink, 6 GHz, indoor rooms (pp. 3, 4, 12).
method: Multi-agent PPO, one agent per beamforming variable, trained with reinforcement learning plus a decaying imitation loss toward SCA solutions; matching, k-means, BCD outside (pp. 10-12).
data_channel: Custom Rician simulator (factor 4 dB, LoS and NLoS paths); only the path loss follows 3GPP TR 38.901 indoor hotspot; random UE positions per episode (p. 12).
test_conditions: Training episodes of 10 slots with random UE positions; testing on the fixed four-room topology of Fig. 6(a), sweeping transmit power 10-50 dBm; no unseen scenario (pp. 12, 14).
baselines: Learned: MAPPO without imitation, single-agent PPO. Non-learned: CA (successive convex approximation), WOA (whale optimization), equal-power allocation (p. 13).
metrics: Cumulative reward and convergence steps, average UE throughput versus transmit power, inference time, clustering time (pp. 13, 14, 16).
complexity: Order O(sum of n_{l-1}n_l) for the networks and a BCD total (p. 12); inference 0.002 s versus 20 s CA and 40 s WOA (pp. 14, 16).
q1_support: p. 12: "The channel between an AP and an UE can be modeled as a Rician channel". Not met: 3GPP TR 38.901 supplies only the path loss ("path loss model for the indoor hotspot scenario"); no CDL/TDL profile, QuaDRiGa or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "Each curve corresponds to a different configuration, with varying numbers of STAR-RIS elements". Not met: these are separate training-convergence curves, Table I (p. 16) gives only inference time, and Fig. 6(c) sweeps transmit power; no trained model is tested on an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 14: "CAMAPPO outperforms CA by 10% and up to 15%, on average" and "PPO also showed about 7% lower performance on average" (average throughput versus power, Fig. 6(c)); p. 13: "PPO: The general PPO approach performs a joint optimization of all beamforming vector variables through a single neural network." MAPPO is an ablation and is not counted.
q4_support: p. 14: "CA and WOA took 20s and 40s, respectively, but inference through network models took 0.002s"; p. 12 gives the complexity order O(sum of n_{l-1}*n_l) of the networks and an overall BCD complexity.
q5_support: p. 12: "UEs are randomly distributed across the rooms during the learning stage". Not met: the data come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link and no public channel dataset appears in the paper.
notes: Area 3: the learned agents output the AP active beamforming vectors and the STAR-RIS amplitude and phase coefficients (Algorithm 4, p. 11; Algorithm 5 line 8, p. 12). User association (many-to-one matching), pairing (k-means) and decoding order are classical (pp. 6-8). q3 rests on single-agent PPO as the standard learning algorithm applied to the same problem (p. 13, Fig. 6(c) on p. 14); MAPPO is an ablation of the proposed CAMAPPO and was not counted, so the reviewer may want to confirm that PPO counts. q2 is 0 because Table I (p. 16) reports only inference time for 18 to 34 users with no performance of a model trained elsewhere, and Fig. 5(c) shows convergence curves per configuration; the reviewer may check this. Perfect CSI is assumed (p. 4).
